clue.text: Loud little boy turned modest

indicators.note: turned means the short boy's name is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: Alf is a short form of the boy's name Alfred
a modest person is shy

explanation.surface: A small boy who was noisy has become quiet and retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes FLA from ALF, a shortened boy's name; 'Loud' looks like a description of the boy but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud clothes are garish and showy, the same sense as flashy.

clue.text: See 24
Most elegant content of baby's nappies, terrifying!

indicators.note: the content of a run of words is the letters held inside it, here across baby's, nappies and terrifying

explanation.surface: A grim joke about what one finds inside a baby's nappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' picks out the letters running from the end of baby's through nappies into the start of terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy is informal for smart and stylish, so the superlative means most smartly turned out.

clue.text: Talk bringing decrease in fish up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
in puts the word for decrease inside the fish

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
to ebb is to decline or decrease, like the tide

explanation.surface: Someone talking about dwindling stocks of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole assembly, which works because this is a down clue; 'bringing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yabber is Australian slang for chatter or idle talk.

clue.text: Record playing in calm, calm water

indicators.note: in tells us the record and playing go inside the word for calm

parts.note: mild weather is calm and gentle
an LP is a long-playing record
a show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: Putting on a record to unwind beside still water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LPON inside MILD, after its L; the repeated 'calm' is one for the wordplay, one in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A millpond is the dammed water feeding a mill, proverbially still and smooth.

clue.text: Problem raised about outfield isn't surprising, given this many errors?

indicators.note: about means the reversed problem goes round the jumbled letters
raised, in a down clue, means the word is turned to read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: surprising suggests the letters of outfield isn't are thrown into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A cricket fielding side keeps dropping catches, and nobody is surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses the problem word in this down clue; 'about' wraps it round the letters 'surprising' jumbles. The outfield is cricket's outer playing area, where catches go down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from the Bible's line that love covers a host of failings, means a great number of faults.

clue.text: Giving great yawns, tedious chore ends

parts.note: great means large

indicators.note: ends asks for the final letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Someone yawning their way through a boring household task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes the last letters of yawns, tedious and chore: S, S, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity, the free bestowing of gifts or money, so a noun for giving.

clue.text: Driver having to edge skyward

indicators.note: skyward, in a down clue, means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the lip of something is its rim or edge

explanation.surface: A motorist forced to inch upward along a precipice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skyward' reverses TOLIP; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is the person at the controls who steers an aircraft or ship.

clue.text: Too unfunny hiding something up one's sleeve — I don't want it!

indicators.note: hiding means the jumbled letters conceal the next item within them
funny, as in peculiar, signals the letters before it are mixed up

parts.note: a handkerchief, or hanky, is traditionally tucked up a sleeve

explanation.surface: A refusal of a not-very-funny joke concealing a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfunny' must be split: its UN joins 'Too' as the fodder, and 'funny' is the anagram signal; 'hiding' then puts the hanky inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite refusal of an offer, said when declining something.

clue.text: Saint high on life, ultimately blessed, starts back in big city

indicators.note: high, as in intoxicated, suggests the letters of saint are scrambled
back means those initial letters are read in reverse order
starts asks for the first letter of each of life, ultimately and blessed

explanation.surface: A saint who is high on life feels blessed at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' scrambles SAINT to ISTAN; 'starts' gives LUB, which 'back' turns into BUL. 'on' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city and one of the most populous in the world.

clue.text: Connect first of ropes and lift

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of ropes

parts.note: to lift someone's spirits is to elate them

explanation.surface: Instructions for rigging: attach a rope and raise it.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate two things is to link or connect them.

clue.text: Article of faith I spoon-feed to fool with solemn declaration

indicators.note: to fool with something is to play about with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenet of faith forced on a gullible person by way of a solemn pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fool with' rearranges all 24 letters of 'Article of faith I spoon-feed'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the formal vow a US president makes on taking up the post, a solemn pledge.

clue.text: Gold stolen by mischievous altar boy — might trial happen here?

indicators.note: stolen by means the gold is taken in by, so placed inside, the jumbled letters
mischievous suggests the letters of altar boy are behaving badly and get rearranged

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A naughty altar boy has pinched the gold; will he face a trial?
explanation.walkthrough: 'mischievous' rearranges ALTAR BOY to LABATORY, and 'stolen by' puts OR inside it. 'trial' looks like a court case but is an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room for scientific work, where experiments and tests are carried out.

clue.text: See 24
Writer's movement finished, author's right significantly advanced?

parts.note: when time is up it is finished

indicators.note: significantly advanced means the letter for right is moved well forward in the author's name

parts.note: Bram Stoker was the author of Dracula

explanation.surface: An author has completed a work with a dramatic shift of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'significantly advanced' moves the R of STOKER from the end forward to make STROKE. The writer of the definition is a pen, not a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstroke is the upward line made by a pen in handwriting.

clue.text: Wine bottles bloke endlessly passed round university, topped up again

indicators.note: bottles means the wine word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: red is a colour of wine

indicators.note: passed round means the shortened bloke goes round the letter for university
endlessly removes the final letter of the word for bloke

parts.note: feller is a colloquial form of fellow, a bloke

explanation.surface: A tale of a man drinking his way round a university with a bottle of red.
explanation.walkthrough: Feller is a colloquial spelling of fellow. 'endlessly' drops its last letter, 'passed round' wraps that round U, and 'bottles' puts the result inside the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuel is to fill a tank with fuel once more, so refuelled means replenished.

clue.text: Adonis lowers bar

parts.note: lowers here are cattle, animals that low or moo, kept for beef
a bar of soap is also called a cake

explanation.surface: A handsome man drops the bar in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowers' is not 'brings down' but things that low, cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, stands for a muscular, good-looking man, informally beefcake.

clue.text: Curtain level in hole

indicators.note: in puts the level inside the hole

parts.note: a pore is a tiny hole in skin
a tier is a level or layer

explanation.surface: A theatre seating plan: a tier with a hole and a curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A portiere is a heavy curtain hung across a doorway.

clue.text: Seeing return of predator, run!

indicators.note: return of means the word for predator is read backwards

parts.note: a wolf is a predator

explanation.surface: A warning cry when the wolf comes back: run!
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like a verb shouted at the reader; it is the noun or verb for a stream's movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that runs flows, so a flow is a run or stream.

clue.text: Blue dressing is cut off

indicators.note: dressing means the word for blue wraps round is, like a garment

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: A blue bandage put on where something has been severed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour of dressing; it means sad, DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown a relative is to reject them and sever all ties.

clue.text: See 11
I see nothing well after turning up for performance

indicators.note: turning up, in a down clue, means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: ah is said on understanding something, like I see
O looks like zero, nothing
oh is an exclamation like well

explanation.surface: Someone realises a performance came to nothing after they arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AHOOH. 'performance' means a fuss, as in 'what a performance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a commotion or fuss, and in British usage a performance is a needless fuss.

clue.text: Dye brown paper, cutting top and bottom

indicators.note: cutting top and bottom, in a down clue, removes the first and last letters

parts.note: manila is the tough brown paper used for envelopes and folders

explanation.surface: Instructions for a craft project: dye brown paper and trim the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting top and bottom' drops the M and A at the ends of MANILA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue colouring made from it.

clue.text: A political clown and jester initially slipping over in oil

indicators.note: slipping over suggests a fall head over heels, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: BoJo is the nickname of the former UK prime minister Boris Johnson, often seen as a clown

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of jester

explanation.surface: A buffoonish politician and a jester take a pratfall in a puddle of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: BoJo is Boris Johnson, former British prime minister. 'slipping over' reverses ABOJOJ; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jojoba is a desert shrub whose seeds yield a liquid wax used as an oil in cosmetics.

clue.text: Whatever Russian collected proving suspicious

indicators.note: proving suspicious, as in turning out dodgy, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Whatever a Russian agent gathered turned out to look fishy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proving suspicious' rearranges all sixteen letters of RUSSIAN COLLECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever, said with a shrug, is a dismissive expression of total indifference.

clue.text: Old pianist, I say, shares playing

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like I say

indicators.note: playing, as in playing about, signals the letters of shares are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an elderly pianist sharing the music.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Myra Hess was a British pianist famed for wartime concerts at the National Gallery. 'playing' rearranges SHARES to RAHESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Myra Hess, who died in 1965, was a celebrated twentieth-century concert pianist.

clue.text: Nut with piece of cake, but different starter

indicators.note: but different starter means the first letter of the word for piece of cake is swapped for another

parts.note: something easy is a doddle, informally in Britain, as in a piece of cake

explanation.surface: A recipe: a nut with a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like a food but means the head. 'different starter' swaps D for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut and noddle are both informal words for the head.
